instructions: 1. Have the piece as a content-pieces row with its script and goes_out date (pour the example rows, or make list:content-pieces from them).
2. Enroll your own voice once so a cloned voiceover is allowed (tool:voices lists it as yours); without it the run chooses another path, such as a recording you already made or text on screen.
3. Say "Run workflow:make-the-piece-without-waiting-for-the-person" with piece_row (and due_at, waiting_on when they differ from the row).
4. Until the due time it waits; if your own recording arrives first it hands the piece back, since your own always wins.
5. After the due time it voices the script in your voice, makes the video, checks it for each place and keeps it as a draft for your approval; it writes the no-wait branch into list:tree-branches.

worked_examples.title: A voiceover past its due time
worked_examples.ask: The training video is waiting on my voiceover; don't wait past Saturday 9 am.
worked_examples.given: The piece row holds the script "You asked how a new baker learns the bake in a morning...", state Being made, and the owner's enrolled voice is listed by tool:voices.
worked_examples.hands_back: paths: cloned voice from the script (needs the enrolled voice, allowed true); an earlier recording that covers it (none found, allowed true); text on screen over b-roll (needs b-roll, allowed true). chosen: cloned voice.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
